source: Episcopal Diocese of Vermont 2026 Prayer Cycle
notes: Source covers Advent Year A (November 30, 2025, “1 Advent”) through Christ the King (November 22, 2026), one complete liturgical year, plus a final “1 Advent (Year B), 11/29/2026: New Cycle of Prayer begins” row with no actual prayer subject printed. The five entries before January 1, 2026 (11/30, 12/7, 12/14, 12/21, 12/28/2025) are included here rather than split into a separate file, matching this corpus's existing precedent for a diocesan cycle whose own declared range spans a year boundary (see e.g. episcopal-california-2026.json, episcopal-nevada-2026.json, episcopal-san-diego-2026.json, episcopal-tennessee-2026.json) -- the source's own document is itself titled “...2026 Prayer Cycle” and the bulk of its 52 dated entries fall in calendar year 2026.

The final row, “1 Advent (Year B)” dated 11/29/2026, prints only “New Cycle of Prayer begins” with no congregation, ministry, or office named -- it is an administrative marker that the diocese's next annual cycle starts that Sunday, not a prayer subject. Excluded from `entries` rather than fabricating a subject for it; disclosed here instead.

Liturgical labels are transcribed in the source's own numbered short form (e.g. “1 Advent”, “2 Epiphany”, “13 Pentecost”) rather than expanded to “First Sunday of Advent” etc. The January 11, 2026 entry's label is printed across two lines in the source's own Dates column (“1 Epiphany” then “The Baptism of Our Lord”, above the date) -- joined here as “1 Epiphany: The Baptism of Our Lord” following this corpus's existing colon-join convention for a source's own two-part liturgical label (see e.g. episcopal-atlanta-2026.json, episcopal-idaho-2026.json).

November 1, 2026 is labeled “All Saints’ Sunday” in the source rather than continuing the ordinary Pentecost numbering (it falls between “22 Pentecost” and “24 Pentecost”, with no “23 Pentecost” printed anywhere) -- this is the source's own substitution of the Principal Feast for the ordinarily-numbered Sunday, not a gap or an error in this transcription.

Typo preserved verbatim per this corpus's standing rule against silently correcting a source: the February 15, 2026 (“6 Epiphany”) entry reads “Minsitry and work of JUMP and Cathedral Square Corporation” (“Minsitry” for “Ministry”), unlike every other week's correctly-spelled “Ministry and work of...” phrasing.

The source's own extracted text mixes a straight apostrophe (') and a curly right-single-quotation-mark (’) across otherwise identical possessive congregation names, inconsistently and sometimes within the very same sentence -- e.g. April 26, 2026 prints “St. James' Church” with a straight mark and “St. Peter’s Church” with a curly mark in the same row; June 14's “St. Luke's” is straight while September 20's “St. Luke’s” is curly. Both forms are preserved exactly as the source's own text encodes them in each instance, never normalized to one style.

September 20, 2026's “St. Alban’s” (the town paired with St. Luke's in that week's constellation) is printed with an apostrophe; the real Vermont town of that name is conventionally spelled “St. Albans” (no apostrophe). Preserved exactly as printed rather than silently corrected.

The source's own “Parishes” column is one continuous descriptive sentence per row, not separate name/place/clergy columns. Where the source uses a semicolon to separate a specifically named congregation from trailing clergy and/or senior-warden identification (e.g. “Christ Church, Bethel; Nancy Wuttke, Senior Warden”), that trailing identification is recorded verbatim in the `parish` subject's own `note` field, following this corpus's existing precedent for the identical situation (see episcopal-south-carolina-2026.json's per-parish clergy notes). Where a comma or “and” instead joins one continuous descriptive phrase naming no separate congregation (e.g. “Ministry and work of the Commission on Ministry, Lisa Schnell, Chairperson”), the full phrase is kept together as a single `category` subject's `name`, unsplit.

Six weeks name a “constellation” (the diocese's own term for a shared-clergy grouping) of two to four congregations under one week, with shared clergy and/or wardens not attributed in the source to any one specific member congregation: April 26 (“The Shires Constellation”, 2 congregations), July 5 (an unnamed “constellation”, 2 congregations), July 19 (“The Upper Valley Constellation”, 4 congregations), August 2 (“The Northeast Kingdom Constellation”, 4 congregations), September 20 and September 27 (each “The Constellation of...” naming 2 congregations). Each named congregation is recorded as its own separate `parish` subject (never merged into one subject or given a single fabricated shared place), with the constellation's own description and the shared, unattributed clergy/wardens repeated in each member congregation's own `note` -- following this corpus's existing precedent for a multi-congregation shared-clergy grouping (see the “Trinity Cluster” entries in episcopal-iowa.json). Where the source names multiple wardens for a multi-congregation week without saying which warden serves which specific congregation (July 5's “Brian Garland, Senior Warden; and Jack Manning, Senior Warden” for two churches), that ambiguity is disclosed in the note rather than guessed at.

April 19, 2026 (“3 Easter”) reads “Church of Our Saviour and the ministries of Mission Farm, Killington; the Rev. Lisa Ransom”. “Mission Farm” is Church of Our Saviour's own retreat/camp ministry at the same Killington location, joined to the parish by “and” rather than by the source's own semicolon delimiter used elsewhere to separate genuinely distinct items -- kept as part of this single `parish` subject's `note` rather than split into a separately-typed subject.

Diocese self-identification: the source document's own page title reads “Episcopal Diocese of Vermont 2026 Prayer Cycle” (without “The”), but its own body text consistently uses the fuller form “The Episcopal Diocese of Vermont” (e.g. “Pray for the People and Ministries of The Episcopal Diocese of Vermont”, and again in several individual entries) -- `diocese` uses this fuller, repeatedly-printed in-body form.

The source is a single continuous two-column table (Dates | Parishes) running across 4 landscape pages, not a multi-column grid of independently-ordered items -- confirmed by rendering all 4 pages as images at 150 DPI and visually comparing every row against the `pdftotext -layout` extraction before transcribing; no column-interleaving risk (of the kind flagged elsewhere in this corpus for genuinely multi-column sources) was found.

The source's own page header also links to the worldwide Anglican Cycle of Prayer (https://www.anglicancommunion.org/resources/cycle-of-prayer/download-the-acp.aspx) as a companion resource, and a “Year A” / “Pray for the People and Ministries of The Episcopal Diocese of Vermont” row serves as the table's own column-group header -- neither is a dated prayer entry, so neither is transcribed into `entries`.
